text.div:
SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD

  • Evaluation: IPSS with the quality-of-life question, bladder scan for post-void residual, urinalysis and urine culture, blood count, creatinine and electrolytes, digital rectal examination, and a kidney and bladder ultrasound for obstruction; a frequency-volume chart once voiding
  • PSA only after shared decision-making: it helps estimate prostate size and choose treatment; screening for prostate cancer is not recommended at his age, and he would not want treatment for a slow-growing cancer; drawn before the catheter is placed, because retention and catheters raise it
  • Indwelling urethral catheter to drain the bladder, with a closed drainage system, the bag below the bladder, daily washing with soap and water, no routine antibiotics or bladder washouts, no treatment of bacteria in the urine without symptoms, a change every four weeks, and same-day review for fever, pain, blood, or a blocked catheter
  • Tamsulosin 0.4 mg at bedtime for at least three days and usually several weeks before a trial without catheter; fall precautions: take it after the evening meal, rise slowly, sit to pass urine at night, and use a night light
  • Urology consultation for chronic urinary retention with a raised creatinine: confirm the cause, judge the risk, plan the trial without catheter, advise on a 5-alpha-reductase inhibitor, and set out the procedures that suit a frail 79-year-old who wants to avoid an operation
  • Medication review with the AGS Beers Criteria: avoid anticholinergic drugs for bladder symptoms while in retention, first-generation antihistamines, and benzodiazepines; avoid nonselective alpha-blockers; review his herbal preparation with the pharmacist for interactions and unlabeled ingredients
  • Monitor on the CMID and AUA schedule: IPSS at every visit once voiding; post-void residual with each trial without catheter and after it; creatinine with retention; PSA at baseline and six months after starting finasteride, doubled for interpretation; response to tamsulosin at four to twelve weeks and to finasteride at three to six months
  • Geriatric assessment before any surgical decision: frailty, gait and falls, orthostatic blood pressure on tamsulosin, cognition, mood, delirium risk, nutrition, and what matters most to him
  • Finasteride 5 mg daily for the 85 mL prostate, with a new PSA baseline after six months (measured value doubled for interpretation); trial without catheter after about six weeks of tamsulosin, once any infection is treated
  • Surgical options counseled after the failed trial without catheter: laser enucleation (HoLEP) recommended for an 85 mL prostate with refractory retention; transurethral resection and simple prostatectomy as alternatives; prostatic artery embolization under local anesthesia as a less invasive option with less durable results; prostatic urethral lift and water vapor therapy less suitable for this size, median lobe, and retention; each weighed against his frailty, delirium risk, and wishes
  • His decision, in his own terms: defer any operation or procedure; keep the catheter, changed every four weeks, with tamsulosin and finasteride; a second trial without catheter after three to four months of finasteride; reconsider prostatic artery embolization, then laser enucleation, if that fails or if infections recur, bleeding, stones, or kidney harm develop; continue his herbal preparation after the pharmacist's review

resource.description: Evaluation and management of lower urinary tract symptoms with urinary retention in a 79-year-old man, on the AUA benign prostatic hyperplasia guideline (2021, amended 2023), the AUA white paper on nonneurogenic chronic urinary retention, and the CMID benign prostatic hyperplasia monograph: the IPSS, post-void residual, urinalysis and culture, creatinine and kidney ultrasound for obstruction, PSA with shared decision-making about what it means at his age, an indwelling catheter with catheter-associated infection prevention and treatment (IDSA 2009), an alpha-blocker before a trial without catheter, a 5-alpha-reductase inhibitor for a large prostate, surgical options (laser enucleation, transurethral resection, and less invasive procedures such as prostatic artery embolization) weighed against frailty, a geriatric assessment (falls with alpha-blockers, delirium risk, cognition) with the AGS Beers Criteria 2023, a goals-of-care conversation, and his own values about surgery and his traditional remedies, recorded in his own terms and respected.
